notes: MMR-33 settlement economy (docs/settlements.md). Owner: SettlementFactory (src/MNBL.ProceduralWorld/Campaign/SettlementFactory.cs). Every value is a quantile of the installed settlements' own distribution at the settlement's percentile among the generated ones, so it stays inside the installed range whatever the world's size. Food stocks, militia, gold, workshops and garrisons follow at new game from these values through the installed behaviours.

streams.rule:
value(stream, version, world prefix, entity, draw) = first 8 bytes of sha256("mnbl.settlement-stream/1
" + stream + "
" + version + "
" + prefix + "
" + entity + "
" + draw), big-endian

towns.rule: the town's percentile of log(population) among the generated towns of its class (small, medium, capital), mapped to the quantile of the matching installed prosperity tercile

castles.rule: the castle's garrison town's percentile of log(population) among the generated towns, mapped to the installed castle prosperity quantile

hearth.rule: a village's share of its town's rural population (rural / villages of the town), its percentile among the generated villages, mapped to the installed hearth quantile

villageTypes.rule: the source production class (farming, fishing, resource, harbor) picks from the village culture's installed village types of that class, weighted by their installed counts, from the villageTypes stream; a culture without that class falls back to all its installed types. A fishing type needs a port (installed: 36 of 36 fishing villages have one): a village without a port draws from its class without the fishing types, else from its culture's farming types

buildings.rule: towns take the median installed building levels of their prosperity tercile (small, medium, capital); castles the median castle levels; a port town adds building_shipyard at the median installed port-town level, an inland town never has one

binding.rule: in order: (1) every village starts at the compiler's bound town; (2) a village farther from its bound settlement than distance.preferredRatio x the world's town spacing is rebound to the nearest town or castle of its land group within that limit, one of its own kingdom first, else of any kingdom; with none it binds to the nearest town or castle of its land group (remote) and must stay within distance.engineTradeRatio x spacing; (3) each castle of a town, in id order, takes its nearest remaining village of that town within the limit and of its land group in turn, until it has castleVillages or the town is down to townMinimum; (4) a castle still below castleVillages takes a village within the limit and of its land group from the towns of its kingdom with more than townMinimum, from the town with the most villages first, then the nearest. A castle without a village, a town without one, a remote village beyond the engine limit, and a castle village with no town of its kingdom within the engine limit (its trade bound) are problems

distance.rule: spacing: the mean periodic distance from each town to its nearest town in the generated world; preferredRatio = installedMaxRatio x tolerance; engineTradeRatio: the engine trade-binds a castle's village to a town within 3 x the average distance between the closest two towns (DefaultVillageTradeModel.TradeBoundDistanceLimitAsDays, installed IL)

installed.note: townMaximum is the installed maximum plus one: a generated world has fewer castles per town to take villages (installed 1.33)

balance.rule: a generated world's villages per fief and hearth per fief stay within band x the installed values, and every town and castle within the binding counts (a town the source gave fewer than townMinimum villages is reported, not refused)

food.rule: a town's trade-area food supply (the daily food production of the villages bound to it and to the castles whose trade bound it is) is at least townMinimum, the smallest installed one; a town below it has its trade-area village with the least food (nearest the town first) redrawn to the most food-producing type its culture allows for its class, else among its culture's farming types (a fishing type only with a port), until it reaches it. Village production scales with hearth in game; the supply compares the types' full production amounts, computed the same way for the installed towns (a castle's villages counted with its nearest town)
food.provenance: DefaultVillageTypes.InitializeAll and AddProductions, NavalVillageTypes.InitializeAll (installed IL); checked in game by the settlement fixture probe

positions.rule: staged (pendingEngineValidation): centre and gate are the MMR-28 settlement point; a port town's port is its MMR-28 port candidate sea point, within the installed port-gate maximum plus one cell from the staged gate (the MMR-28 engine envelope installedPortGateMax 10.97; the installed port-centre maximum is 6.96); a harbour village's port is the centre of its MMR-28 harbour cell (a navigable sea cell), within the installed village port-centre maximum plus one cell; MMR-40 places gates and ports on the engine navmesh and MMR-35 compiles the landing metadata

texts.hideout: An outlaw hideout in the wilds.

hideouts.rule: SettlementFactory builds a hideout from a placed specification (bandit culture, position) with a prototype of that bandit culture; placing hideouts across a world is MMR-34's (bandits and hideouts)
